Implementation Plan

Plan for #6889 (fix for the orchestrate-poll group 3 shard failure, PR #6881 lineage)

Planning ref: `git rev-parse HEAD` = `de45b6cf454f106c197dd3cc00a499324619ad6c`, symbolic branch `main`. No integration branch metadata, so there is no mismatch. The fix PR targets `main` (Q2: A).

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends the existing `shard_failures` loop in the `Orchestrate poll process unit tests` step of `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, and the existing `run_shard_judge` / `ShardJudgeTest` harness in `tests/test_ci_poll_test_sharding.py`
Scope-mode justification: The clarification answers chose Q1 = A+B (option C) and Q2 = A. The work therefore has two parts. First, try to reproduce the group 3 failure locally and fix any test that fails every time. Second, make the CI step print the names of failing tests outside the collapsed `::group::` blocks, so the next triage can see them in the log tail. Pass/fail behaviour stays exactly as it is. The release gates (`mark-stable.yml`, `test-and-mark-stable.yml`) contain the same shard loop. Copying the summary into them would add two automation-path files that the answer's `files_touched` contract does not list, so they are left alone (see D2). Completeness inside the approved scope is kept: shards with no log and shards with no `.rc` file also get a summary line, and a failure line with no recoverable test name is still reported. Under §6, Correctness & safety means the gate keeps its exact semantics; Operational clarity is the purpose of the change.

---

1. Files likely to change

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: the `Orchestrate poll process unit tests` step in the `orchestrate-poll` matrix job, currently lines 1416–1443 (the `shard_failures=0` loop through `exit 1`). This file is about 66 KB, far below the 480,000-byte guard.
- `tests/test_ci_poll_test_sharding.py`: extend `PollStepContractTest` and `ShardJudgeTest`. Do not create a new file.
- `changelog.d/6889-orchestrate-poll-shard-failure-summary.md`: new fragment, following CLAUDE.md §20.
- Conditional: change these only if the local reproduction below shows a test failing every time.
  - `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py`
  - `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`

files_touched:

(The last two entries only allow edits. The implementer must not touch them unless reproduction step R3 below shows a concrete failure that points at that file.)

2. Functions and modules to implement

A. Reproduction (no code unless something fails every time)

- R1: Rebuild the test lists the way CI does.
  - Run the Python block from the `Derive orchestrate poll test subsets` step (ci.yml ~1304–1333).
  - It parses `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py` with `ast`, keeps the top-level `test_*` functions, and sorts them.
  - It drops the `test_implementation_failed_*` fast-fail set.
  - It writes the rest to `/tmp/orchestrate_poll_remaining_tests.txt`.
- R2: Take group 3 of 4 with `awk -v n=3 -v total=4 'NR % total == n' /tmp/orchestrate_poll_remaining_tests.txt > /tmp/g3.txt`.
- R3: Run `mapfile -t t < /tmp/g3.txt; PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py "${t[@]}"` and record every `  FAIL  <name>: ...` line. To match CI's local split exactly, also run each of the 4 slices `awk -v n=<s> -v total=4 'NR % total == n' /tmp/g3.txt` separately.
- R4: If a test fails every time, fix the cause it demonstrates, in the test or in `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`, whichever the failure points at. Do not skip, weaken, retry or xfail the test.
- R5: If nothing reproduces, do not change the test or poller files. Say in the PR body that group 3 passed locally on `de45b6cf`, and list which slices ran.
- Mark any validator the sandbox cannot run as UNVERIFIED. The final check is the fix PR's own `orchestrate-poll (3)` CI job.

B. Observability: changes to the shard loop in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`

- Before the loop, next to `shard_failures=0`, declare a new array `shard_failure_summaries=()`. Grep confirms neither name exists in the step today.
- Shard with tests but no log (the existing `produced no log` branch): before `continue`, append `orchestrate-poll shard ${shard} exit none failed tests: no log (tests did not run)`.
- `shard_rc -ne 0` branch: keep the existing in-loop `::error::orchestrate-poll shard ${shard} failed (exit ${shard_rc})` line unchanged, then build the summary:
  - Pull the names from the log, deduped and capped at 20:
    ```
    failed_names="$(grep -E '^  FAIL  [A-Za-z0-9_]+:' "/tmp/poll_shard_${shard}.log" | sed -E 's/^  FAIL  ([A-Za-z0-9_]+):.*/\1/' | awk '!seen[$0]++' || true)"
    ```
  - The `|| true` is required. The step runs under `set -euo pipefail`, so a `grep` that finds nothing would otherwise abort the step before the gate.
  - Count the names. If there are more than 20, keep the first 20, join them with `, `, and append ` (+K more)`.
  - If there are no names, use `no FAIL lines (process failure)`.
  - Append `orchestrate-poll shard ${shard} exit ${shard_rc} failed tests: ${names}` to `shard_failure_summaries`.
  - Name the new locals so they don't collide with anything in the step, e.g. `shard_failed_names` and `shard_failed_count`.
- Inside the existing `if [ "${shard_failures}" -ne 0 ]; then` block, before the existing `::error::${shard_failures} orchestrate-poll shard(s) failed.` line, loop over `shard_failure_summaries` and print each entry as `::error::<entry>`.
  - These lines sit outside every `::group::` and at the end of the step, so they land in the log tail and the job annotations.
  - The tally line stays the last line before `exit 1`.
  - Placing them inside this `if` block keeps them inside the slice that `run_shard_judge` cuts out (`shard_failures=0` … the `\nfi\n` after the tally), so the test exercises the real shell.
- Unchanged: the partition `awk` expressions, `shard_failures` counting, the no-log and missing/non-numeric `.rc` handling, the reap-before-judge loop, `exit 1`, and the group-0 single-file modules.

C. Contract tests in `tests/test_ci_poll_test_sharding.py`

- `PollStepContractTest`:
  - New test asserting that in `self.run` the summary print (`shard_failure_summaries`) comes after the shard loop's `done` and before both the `orchestrate-poll shard(s) failed.` tally and `exit 1`.
  - The existing partition and failure-handling tests stay untouched and must keep passing.
- `ShardJudgeTest` (summary cases run only against the `ci` step run; see D2). New tests:
  - A shard with log `"  PASS  test_a\n  FAIL  test_b: boom\n2 passed, 1 failed, 3 total\n"` and rc `1`:
    - return code is 1;
    - stdout contains `::error::orchestrate-poll shard 1 exit 1 failed tests: test_b`;
    - that line comes after the `::endgroup::` of the last shard and before `1 orchestrate-poll shard(s) failed.`
  - A shard with rc `1` and no FAIL lines gets `no FAIL lines (process failure)`.
  - A shard with no log gets `exit none failed tests: no log (tests did not run)`.
  - 25 FAIL lines are capped to 20 names plus ` (+5 more)`.
  - A FAIL line containing `::warning::` or other characters outside `[A-Za-z0-9_]` in the failure text never shows that text in the summary; only the sanitized name appears.
  - All shards green: no `failed tests:` line and return code 0. This extends `test_all_shards_green_passes`.
- The existing `ShardJudgeTest` cases keep running against all three workflows. The release copies are unchanged, so they still pass.

D. Changelog fragment

- `changelog.d/6889-orchestrate-poll-shard-failure-summary.md`, following CLAUDE.md §20: a user-facing sentence saying CI now names the failing orchestrate-poll tests in the log tail when a shard fails, and that pass/fail is unchanged.

3. Data structures affected

- New bash array `shard_failure_summaries` and new locals `shard_failed_names` / `shard_failed_count`, all local to one CI step.
- No state, schema, label, marker or env var changes.

4. API / interface changes

- None for callers. The CI log gains extra `::error::` annotation lines, but only when a shard has already failed.
- Existing log strings are kept byte-for-byte:
  - `orchestrate-poll shard N failed (exit rc)`
  - `orchestrate-poll shard N produced no log; its tests did not run`
  - `N orchestrate-poll shard(s) failed.`
- check-failure-triage and the existing tests read these strings.

## Decisions

### D1 — Where the failure summary is printed
- Chosen: collect one entry per failed shard inside the existing judgment loop, then print them as `::error::` lines inside the existing `if [ "${shard_failures}" -ne 0 ]` block, right before the tally line and `exit 1`.
- Alternatives considered: (a) add test names to the existing in-loop `failed (exit rc)` line; (b) add a separate post-step `if: failure()` step that re-reads `/tmp/poll_shard_*.log`; (c) write to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` only.
- Why:
  - The in-loop line is printed between collapsed groups, so it scrolls out of the tail triage reads.
  - A separate step adds a new step and a new contract surface.
  - The step summary is not part of the log tail.
  - Printing inside the existing block keeps the gate identical and stays inside the `run_shard_judge` slice, so the real shell is tested.

### D2 — Release-gate copies of the shard loop
- Chosen: change only `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. Leave the identical loops in `mark-stable.yml` and `test-and-mark-stable.yml` unchanged. Summary assertions target only the `ci` step run.
- Alternatives considered: add the same summary to all three workflows for parity.
- Why:
  - The clarification execution plan limits `files_touched` to `ci.yml` and the sharding test.
  - Each extra `.github/` path needs its own automation-path grant.
  - Check-failure triage reads PR CI logs, not release-gate logs.
